text:
Minnesota visits Edmonton tonight with the model giving the Wild a slight edge in expected goals (3.02 to 2.79), a measure of chance quality. At five on five, the teams are close: MIN has taken 53% of the expected goals in its games, EDM 52%. The Wild create more (3.65 expected goals per 60 minutes against 2.94), while the Oilers allow fewer (2.49 against 2.78). On special teams, EDM's penalty kill allows 0.51 expected goals per game to MIN's 0.67, and the power plays are nearly even, 0.76 for MIN and 0.78 for EDM. The Wild are without Jared Spurgeon (upper body).

Both teams are 4-1-0 in their last five, but they got there differently. MIN held 61% of the expected goals in those games and won the chance battle in four of five. EDM held 49%, and the Oilers' results are running ahead of their chances: a +13 goal difference against +3.6 expected. This is game one of a five-game road trip for Minnesota, who won all three meetings last season.

In net, projected starter Jesper Wallstedt (MIN) is at +6.4 goals saved above expected this season (how many more goals he's stopped than an average goalie would on the same shots), after +5.8 over 35 games last year. Projected EDM starter Devon Levi is at -0.6 this season, with no games last season. Kirill Kaprizov has a 47% chance to score and 75% to record a point, with a six-game point streak, though the model flags him as due to cool. Connor McDavid is at 88% for a point, but his 23 points in eight games are mostly bounces. Evan Bouchard's hot run is likewise mostly bounces, and the model doesn't price it.
